# Rule catalog

<!-- Generated by `npm run docs:gen`. Do not edit by hand. -->

34 rules. "Verified on" is the date the message format was checked against real tool output; "not verified" means the format comes from documentation or knowledge of the tool and has not been checked against a real run, so treat matches with extra care.

Fixtures for every rule are synthetic and written by hand; passing them does not measure accuracy on real logs.

## Source notes

### `config.missing-env`

Wordings follow the GitHub Actions toolkit ("Input required and not supplied") and common application messages; not checked against real runs in this project. Confidence is limited to medium/low because a log cannot prove a secret is empty.

### `docker.build-failed`

BuildKit "failed to solve: process ... did not complete successfully" wording was not checked against real docker output in this project (docker was not available); confidence is capped at medium.

### `docker.copy-not-found`

BuildKit "failed to compute cache key ... not found" and the legacy "COPY failed: file not found in build context" wordings were not checked against real docker output in this project.

### `docker.rate-limit`

The "toomanyrequests" error code and "pull rate limit" wording were not checked against a real registry response in this project.

### `generic.exit-code`

Line "##[error]Process completed with exit code N." observed in a real GitHub Actions log.

### `git.checkout-submodule`

Checked against real git 2.37 output: "fatal: No url found for submodule path ... in .gitmodules" and "fatal: repository ... not found" / "remote: Repository not found.". The "clone of ... into submodule path ... failed" wording was not checked against a real run.

### `git.permission-denied`

Git messages "Permission denied (publickey)", "remote: Permission to ... denied", "Authentication failed", "could not read Username" were not checked against real runs in this project.

### `github.rate-limit`

Wording "API rate limit exceeded" / "secondary rate limit" follows the GitHub REST rate-limit documentation (checked 2026-10-15) but was not seen in a real log here; confidence is capped at medium.

### `github.token-permissions`

GitHub API error message "Resource not accessible by integration"; not checked against a real run in this project.

### `infra.disk-full`

POSIX/Node.js message "ENOSPC: no space left on device" / "No space left on device"; not checked against a real run in this project. The inotify variant (ENOSPC: System limit for number of file watchers reached) is deliberately excluded.

### `infra.job-cancelled`

GitHub Actions cancellation lines ("The operation was canceled.", "Canceling since a higher priority waiting request ... exists") were not checked against real runs in this project.

### `infra.job-timeout`

GitHub Actions message "The job running on runner ... has exceeded the maximum execution time of N minutes" was not checked against a real run in this project.

### `infra.network`

ETIMEDOUT / ECONNRESET / EAI_AGAIN are standard system error codes; these codes were not checked against a real failing run in this project, and their presence says a network call failed, not which side was at fault, so confidence is capped at medium.

### `infra.oom.exit-137`

Exit code 137 is 128 + SIGKILL (9) by shell convention; this was not verified against a real run, and whether the kill came from the out-of-memory killer is NOT visible in the log, so confidence is capped at medium.

### `infra.oom.node-heap`

V8 fatal error text "JavaScript heap out of memory"; not checked against a real run in this project.

### `node.engines`

npm EBADENGINE (with engine-strict) checked against real npm 10.9.0 output. The pnpm (ERR_PNPM_UNSUPPORTED_ENGINE) and Yarn 1 ("The engine ... is incompatible with this module") wordings were not checked against real runs. A plain "npm warn EBADENGINE" is only a warning and is deliberately ignored.

### `node.eslint.problems`

Checked against real ESLint 10.12.0 default ("stylish") formatter output. Other formatters are not covered.

### `node.module-not-found`

Checked against real Node 22 output for require() and import of a missing package. The Jest variant ("Cannot find module ... from ...") was not checked against a real run, so it is reported with medium confidence.

### `node.node-gyp`

node-gyp "gyp ERR!" lines were not checked against a real failing build in this project; confidence is capped at medium.

### `node.npm.auth`

Message format "npm error code E401|E403" follows the same prefix as the verified E404 output; the exact wording of the following lines was not checked against a real registry response.

### `node.npm.ci-lock-mismatch`

Checked against real npm 10.9.0 output (npm ci with a modified package.json, and npm ci without a lockfile).

### `node.npm.e404`

Checked against real npm 10.9.0 output (npm install of a non-existent package).

### `node.npm.eacces`

EACCES is a Node.js/POSIX error code; the surrounding npm message format was not checked against a real run.

### `node.npm.eresolve`

Checked against real npm 10.9.0 output (npm install with conflicting peer dependencies) and a real GitHub Actions npm ci failure (peer range containing spaces).

### `node.pnpm.lockfile`

Checked against real pnpm 10 output (pnpm install --frozen-lockfile after editing package.json).

### `node.prettier.check`

Checked against real Prettier 3.9.10 output of "prettier --check".

### `node.test.failures`

Vitest 5.0.4 output checked against a real run. The Jest output format ("FAIL file", "Tests: N failed") follows Jest documentation and was not checked against a real run.

### `node.test.snapshot`

Vitest 5.0.4 "Snapshot `name` mismatched" checked against a real run. Jest wording ("Snapshot name:", "Snapshots: N failed") follows Jest documentation and was not checked against a real run.

### `node.test.timeout`

Vitest 5.0.4 "Test timed out in Nms." checked against a real run. Jest ("Exceeded timeout of N ms for a test") and Mocha ("Timeout of Nms exceeded.") wording follows their documentation and was not checked against a real run.

### `node.typescript.errors`

Checked against real tsc 6.0.3 output ("file(line,col): error TSxxxx: message"). The "--pretty" variant ("file:line:col - error TSxxxx") follows the TypeScript documentation and was not checked against a real run.

### `node.yarn.lockfile`

Yarn 1.22 message checked against real output. The Yarn Berry message (YN0028) was not checked against a real run, so it is reported with medium confidence.

### `python.import-error`

ModuleNotFoundError checked against real pytest 9.1.1 output on Python 3.14. The "ImportError: cannot import name" wording was not checked against a real run, so it is reported with medium confidence.

### `python.pip.dependency`

The "Could not find a version" / "No matching distribution" messages were checked against real pip output (Python 3.14). The dependency-conflict wording (ResolutionImpossible / "conflicting dependencies") was not checked against a real run, so it is reported with medium confidence.

### `python.pytest.failures`

Checked against real pytest 9.1.1 output (short test summary and final summary line).
